title: Farm Psychology Research Synthesis 2026-09
purpose: Expand the Farm/Sektur/Swamp corpus with evidence-backed psychology, Christian moral vocabulary, attention dynamics, role inversions and research questions. The file is intentionally non-diagnostic: it studies mechanisms and observable patterns rather than assigning psychiatric labels to people.
core_axiom: Within the project's theological vocabulary, every Farmer and Dog encounters a moral choice about the neighbour: preserve personhood or convert the neighbour into material for attention, status, money, belonging, entertainment or revenge. 'Selling the neighbour' is a symbolic name for this conversion.

epistemic_layers.empirical: Observable behavior, public statements, archival counts, platform mechanics and published research.
epistemic_layers.psychological: Mechanisms that research shows can influence behavior or group dynamics; these are hypotheses when applied to a particular person.
epistemic_layers.theological: Christian and Potatoist symbolic interpretation; not empirical proof of supernatural causes.
epistemic_layers.project_vocabulary: Farmer, Dog, Cow, Milk, Mud, Farm, Sektur and Tree of Strife are analytical terms created or adopted by the project.

research_findings.finding: Moral disengagement can convert harmful conduct into apparently acceptable conduct.
research_findings.farm_translation: 'Exposure', 'documentation', 'community defense' or 'just jokes' can function as moral justifications; group participation can diffuse responsibility.

research_findings.finding: Online settings can facilitate moral disengagement through reduced social-emotional cues, easy dissemination and audience dynamics.
research_findings.farm_translation: The distance between actor and target can make humiliation, pile-ons and repeated circulation easier to rationalize.
research_findings.source: Almeida et al. review on online moral disengagement and cyber-aggression

research_findings.finding: Anonymity can increase trolling under experimental conditions.
research_findings.farm_translation: Do not assume a fixed 'bad personality' explains every Dog/Farmer behavior; platform affordances and identifiability can alter conduct.

research_findings.finding: Sadism was positively associated with trolling in one experiment, while psychopathy was not associated in that study.
research_findings.farm_translation: Do not casually diagnose psychopathy from trolling; research supports a more specific and cautious interpretation.

research_findings.finding: The seven deadly sins have been used in psychological scholarship as a taxonomy of temptation domains.
research_findings.farm_translation: Pride, greed, envy, wrath, lust, gluttony and sloth can be used as moral/psychological lenses without pretending they are psychiatric diagnoses.

research_findings.finding: DARVO can affect how observers perceive responsibility and victim credibility.
research_findings.farm_translation: Record denial, attack and reversal as a sequence with evidence rather than treating DARVO as a personality label.

farmer_shadow_map.shadow: archive becomes authority; accumulation substitutes for understanding
asymmetric standards; receipts become weapons rather than tests
compulsive attention hidden behind claimed indifference
belonging becomes a scarce status resource

dog_shadow_map.shadow: obedience and inability to criticize the pack

demon_archetypes.name: The Seller
demon_archetypes.farm_signal: attention, status or money is extracted from another person's degradation

demon_archetypes.name: The Prosecutor
demon_archetypes.temptation: turn moral knowledge into unlimited punishment
demon_archetypes.farm_signal: the original offense stops mattering because the sentence has become the content

demon_archetypes.name: The Mirror
demon_archetypes.temptation: attack externally what remains unresolved internally
demon_archetypes.farm_signal: obsession with a target trait that mirrors the observer's own fear or status anxiety

demon_archetypes.name: The Crowd
demon_archetypes.farm_signal: 'we all did it' becomes moral permission

demon_archetypes.name: The Mask
demon_archetypes.farm_signal: harm is performed and then denied as unserious

demon_archetypes.name: The Hunger
demon_archetypes.temptation: never allow the cycle to end

demon_archetypes.name: The Inverter
demon_archetypes.farm_signal: revenge becomes justice; obsession becomes vigilance; humiliation becomes truth

cult_structure_measurements.use: structural comparison only, never an automatic cult diagnosis
cult_structure_measurements.countermeasure: Measure whether members can disagree, leave, correct leaders, access outside information and maintain relationships outside the group.

biblical_dog_crosswalk.theme: watchmen who fail; dogs that cannot/will not bark

hawkins_crosswalk.sequence: Shame -> Guilt -> Apathy -> Grief -> Fear -> Desire -> Anger -> Pride -> Courage -> Neutrality -> Willingness -> Acceptance -> Reason -> Love -> Joy -> Peace
hawkins_crosswalk.research_question: Which state does the interaction repeatedly reward?
hawkins_crosswalk.rule: Never assign a Hawkins number to a real person as if it were a validated psychological measurement.

new_concepts_to_propagate: documentation has a stopping condition; extraction does not
archive size is not truth; it measures attention infrastructure
the most dangerous inversion is when vice is experienced as virtue
a Dog can manufacture the conditions that justify continued vigilance
a Farmer can become dependent on the existence of the subject they document
the Farm can become independent of the original Cow once secondary creators generate enough material
death changes a Farm from live reaction ecology toward historical archive ecology
repair and disengagement must be measured as seriously as escalation
